title: Two pointers
short: Walk in from both ends to skip checking every pair.
what: Keep two indexes into the same list, often one at each end. Look at the two values, then move one pointer based on what you see. Each move throws away options that cannot work, so you check n things instead of every pair.
analogy: Two people with a sorted price list trying to spend exactly 10 dollars. If the total is too high, the one holding the expensive end steps down. Too low, the cheap end steps up.

frames.label: sum to 10
frames.say: The list is sorted. Find two numbers that add up to 10. L starts at the smallest, R at the biggest.

frames.label: sum to 10
frames.say: 1 + 11 = 12, too big. Even the smallest number is too much for 11, so 11 is out. Move R left.

frames.label: sum to 10
frames.say: 1 + 8 = 9, too small. Even the biggest number left is not enough for 1, so 1 is out. Move L right.

frames.label: sum to 10
frames.say: 4 + 6 = 10. Found at indexes 2 and 3 after 5 checks. Trying every pair would take up to 15.

when: The input is sorted (or you can sort it)
Find a pair or triple with a target sum
Is it a palindrome? Compare the ends
cost: Find a pair in a sorted list
watch: The move rule only works if the list is sorted. Sorting first costs O(n log n).
Use left < right, so a number is never paired with itself.
If the list is not sorted and you need indexes, a dict (hash map) is usually better.
